findings.title: CLAUDE.md drift: Data Flow lists Alignment before Reduction (contradicts the canonical pipeline order and the fitted Pipeline's actual step order), Plot Module omits hyper_animation.py, and 'plot() returns a matplotlib Figure' is unqualified
findings.description: (a) CLAUDE.md 'Data Flow' lists '2. Normalization 3. Alignment ... 4. Dimensionality Reduction ... 5. Clustering', i.e. align before reduce. The canonical order documented in docs/pipeline_order.rst, docs/api.rst, and hypertools/tools/analyze.py ('manip -> normalize -> reduce -> align -> cluster') has reduce BEFORE align, and was verified empirically: analyze(data, reduce='PCA', ndims=3, align='hyper', normalize='across', return_model=True) yields a fitted Pipeline with step order ['normalize', 'reduce', 'align']. (b) CLAUDE.md's Plot Module file list omits hypertools/plot/hyper_animation.py (present on disk) and the HyperAnimation export. (c) CLAUDE.md states twice that 'plot() returns a matplotlib Figure' without qualifying that animate=... returns a HyperAnimation (tuple subclass) and return_model=True returns a dict. All other spot-checked CLAUDE.md architecture claims verified accurate (per-folder module listings, draw.py 3-line shim, dev-extra exclusions, testpaths).

findings.title: hyp.reduce with default ndims=None silently no-ops and returns model=None, while the docstring promises the fitted Reducer for return_model=True
findings.description: reduce(x, 'PCA', return_model=True) (ndims defaulting to None) returns the input UNCHANGED ((50,8) -> (50,8), allclose True) paired with model=None -- for 'PCA', 'IncrementalPCA', and 'UMAP' alike. The docstring says 'return_model : bool -- If True, also return the fitted model: the fitted Reducer wrapper when only the reduce stage ran', and 'ndims : int -- Number of dimensions to reduce' never states that None (the default) means no reduction runs at all. A scientist writing `xr, model = hyp.reduce(x, 'PCA', return_model=True); model.transform(y)` gets AttributeError on NoneType, and gets unreduced data with no warning. With ndims=3 the fitted hypertools.reduce.common.Reducer is returned correctly.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; x=np.random.randn(50,8); r,m=hyp.reduce(x,'PCA',return_model=True); print(np.asarray(r).shape, np.allclose(np.asarray(r),x), type(m))"
findings.expected: either documented ('ndims=None performs no reduction; the model slot is None') or a warning / a sensible default reduction
findings.actual: no-ndims reduced shape: (50, 8) | identical to input: True; PCA -> tuple len 2 | [1]: <class 'NoneType'> (also IncrementalPCA, UMAP); PCA ndims=3 -> [1]: <class 'hypertools.reduce.common.Reducer'>

findings.title: Docstring Parameters coverage gaps across public API: plot() elev/azim undocumented; manip()'s five cross-stage kwargs, cluster()/analyze() random_state, procrustes() format_data, df2mat() return_labels undocumented
findings.description: Systematic inspect.signature-vs-numpydoc sweep of all 35 documented public callables (after manually eliminating parser false positives from grouped headers like 'marker(s) :' and 'duration (animation only) :'): (1) hypertools.plot signature has elev=10, azim=-60 but 'elev' appears NOWHERE in the 57,877-char docstring and 'azim' only inside prose about rotations -- neither is a documented parameter; (2) hypertools.manip's signature accepts normalize/reduce/ndims/align/cluster cross-stage kwargs but its Parameters section documents none of them (its siblings normalize/reduce/align/cluster document theirs); (3) cluster() and analyze() have random_state in signature, not in Parameters; (4) align.procrustes has format_data param undocumented; (5) tools.df2mat has return_labels undocumented. All confirmed against live inspect.signature output.

UNDOC:[align, cluster, ndims, normalize, reduce]'; 'hypertools.cluster ... UNDOC:[random_state]'; 'hypertools.analyze ... UNDOC:[random_state]'; 'hypertools.align.procrustes ... UNDOC:[format_data]'; 'hypertools.tools.df2mat ... UNDOC:[return_labels]'

findings.title: hypertools.save docs page is a single sentence with no Parameters/Returns, and its **kwargs are silently discarded (protocol=5 ignored)
findings.description: save()'s entire docstring is 'Pickle `obj` to `fname`.' -- the autodoc page hypertools.save renders with no Parameters section for a top-level API function. Worse, the signature advertises **kwargs but the body is `pickle.dump(obj, f)` -- kwargs are never forwarded, so hyp.save(obj, 'f.pkl', protocol=5) silently ignores protocol (verified: save({'a':1}, f, protocol=5, banana='x') raises nothing, file written with default protocol). Users reasonably expect pickle kwargs to pass through or an error for unknown kwargs.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp, tempfile, os; f=os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(),'t.pkl'); hyp.save({'a':1}, f, protocol=5, banana='x'); print('no error raised')"
findings.expected: numpydoc Parameters/Returns on save(); kwargs forwarded to pickle.dump (or **kwargs removed / unknown kwargs rejected)

findings.title: api.rst Pipeline blurb says the fitted Pipeline is returned 'when more than one pipeline stage runs' -- a single-stage plot also returns a Pipeline
findings.description: docs/api.rst: 'hypertools.Pipeline is the fitted-model object returned by return_model=True when more than one pipeline stage runs (GH #227 #161)'. Verified that hyp.plot(x, reduce='PCA', return_model=True) -- one explicit stage -- already returns bundle['pipeline'] of type hypertools.core.pipeline.Pipeline. The qualifier is inaccurate (harmlessly so for plot; for standalone reduce the single-stage return is the bare Reducer, so the sentence conflates two behaviors).
findings.repro: env MPLBACKED=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; b=hyp.plot(np.random.randn(50,8), reduce='PCA', return_model=True, show=False); print(type(b['pipeline']))"
findings.expected: wording that matches both plot (always Pipeline in bundle) and standalone dispatchers (bare model when only one stage ran)

findings.title: describe(max_dims=14) on 8-feature data silently plots components 2-13 with correlations flatlined at 1.0 past the true dimensionality
findings.description: Running the README Describe snippet verbatim on 8-dimensional synthetic data (hyp.describe(list_of_arrays, reduce='PCA', max_dims=14)) produces a curve whose x-axis runs to 13 'Number of components' even though the data have only 8 features; values past 8 flatline at correlation 1.0. No warning is emitted that max_dims exceeds the data dimensionality. A scientist could misread the plot as evidence the data support >8 meaningful components. (README's own example uses max_dims=14, inviting exactly this call pattern.)
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; d=[np.random.randn(60,8)+i for i in range(3)]; hyp.describe(d, reduce='PCA', max_dims=14, show=False)"
findings.expected: x-axis capped at data dimensionality, or a UserWarning that max_dims > n_features
findings.actual: evidence PNG shows x-axis 2..13 for 8-feature data, correlation pinned at 1.00 from 8 onward; only warning emitted is the generic 'When input data is large, this computation can take a long time.'
